records.citation: Zhao Y, Zhang C. A review on the novelty measurements of academic papers. Scientometrics 130:727-753.
records.evidence_note: Recent review used to seed and check the census; no metric is admitted solely because it appears in this review.

records.citation: Shibayama S, et al. Identify novel elements of knowledge with word embedding. PLOS ONE 18:e0284567.
records.evidence_note: Explicitly separates element from recombinant novelty and validates element-distance scores with author survey responses.

records.citation: Uzzi B, Mukherjee S, Stringer M, Jones B. Atypical combinations and scientific impact. Science 342:468-472.
records.evidence_note: Canonical atypicality-tail and conventionality-centre profile; its Monte Carlo null and journal units must not be silently replaced.

records.citation: Lee Y-N, Walsh JP, Wang J. Creativity in scientific teams: Unpacking novelty and impact. Research Policy 44:684-697.
records.evidence_note: Original paper-level Novelty U/commonness lower-tail family.

records.citation: Wang J, Veugelers R, Stephan P. Bias against novelty in science. Research Policy 46:1416-1436.
records.evidence_note: Defines first-time combination incidence and distance-weighted variants; later validation is mixed.

records.citation: Matsumoto K, Shibayama S, Kang B, Igami M. Introducing a novelty indicator for scientific research: validating the knowledge-based combinatorial approach. Scientometrics 126:6891-6915.
records.evidence_note: Defines reference-set overlap novelty and validates it against researcher assessments.

records.citation: Bornmann L, Tekles A, Zhang HH, Ye FY. Do we measure novelty when we analyze unusual combinations of cited references? Journal of Informetrics 13:100979.
records.evidence_note: F1000Prime validation supports Novelty U more consistently than first-time-combination W.

records.citation: Fontana M, Iori M, Montobbio F, Sinatra R. New and atypical combinations: an assessment of novelty and interdisciplinarity. Research Policy 49:104063.
records.evidence_note: Finds sensitivity to knowledge units and substantial overlap with interdisciplinarity; prevents diversity measures from being relabeled as novelty.

records.citation: Mishra S, Torvik VI. Quantifying conceptual novelty in the biomedical literature. D-Lib Magazine 22(9/10).
records.evidence_note: Defines time and volume novelty for MeSH concepts and concept combinations.

records.citation: Yan Y, Tian S, Zhang J. The impact of a paper's new combinations and new components on its citation. Scientometrics 122:895-913.
records.evidence_note: Separates never-before-seen components from never-before-seen component pairs.

records.citation: Shibayama S, Yin D, Matsumoto K. Measuring novelty in science with word embedding. PLOS ONE 16:e0254034.
records.evidence_note: Measures semantic distance among cited references and validates against author self-reports.

records.citation: Luo Z, Lu W, He J, Wang Y. Combination of research questions and methods: a new measurement of scientific novelty. Journal of Informetrics 16:101282.
records.evidence_note: Defines temporal/frequency and semantic novelty for question terms, method terms, and their combinations.

records.citation: Leahey E, Lee J, Funk RJ. What types of novelty are most disruptive? American Sociological Review 88:562-597.
records.evidence_note: Operationalizes new methods, theories, and results from author essays; these are contribution loci, not new bibliometric mechanisms.

records.citation: Dirk L. A measure of originality: the elements of science. Social Studies of Science 29:765-776.
records.evidence_note: Classifies originality by whether hypotheses, methods, and results are new or previously reported.

records.citation: Guetzkow J, Lamont M, Mallard G. What is originality in the humanities and the social sciences? American Sociological Review 69:190-212.
records.evidence_note: Shows that contribution loci vary by field and include approach, theory, method, data, topic, and findings.

records.citation: Barlösius E. Concepts of originality in the natural science, medical, and engineering disciplines: an analysis of research proposals. Science, Technology, & Human Values 44:915-937.
records.evidence_note: Supports field-sensitive contribution loci; it does not supply a scalable publication-level formula.

records.citation: Shi F, Evans J. Surprising combinations of research contents and contexts are related to impact. Nature Communications 14:1641.
records.evidence_note: Operationalizes expectation violation in content-context combinations.

records.citation: Jeon D, Lee J, Ahn JM, Lee C. Measuring the novelty of scientific publications: a fastText and local outlier factor approach. Journal of Informetrics 17:101450.
records.evidence_note: Whole-document semantic outlier family using fastText and local outlier factor.

records.citation: Packalen M, Bhattacharya J. Age and the trying out of new ideas. Journal of Human Capital 13:341-373.
records.evidence_note: Uses the age of biomedical idea phrases as a text-based new-idea signal.

records.citation: Arts S, Melluso N, Veugelers R. Beyond citations: measuring novel scientific ideas and their impact in publication text. Review of Economics and Statistics.
records.evidence_note: Text-based origin of new ideas is admissible at T0; follow-on reuse and impact components are not.

records.citation: Hou J, Wang D, Li J. A new method for measuring the originality of academic articles based on knowledge units in semantic networks. Journal of Informetrics 16:101306.
records.evidence_note: Semantic-network knowledge-unit originality family.

records.citation: Amplayo RK, Hong S, Song M. Network-based approach to detect novelty of scholarly literature. Information Sciences 422:542-557.
records.evidence_note: Network expectation and link-based novelty family.

records.citation: Foster JG, Rzhetsky A, Evans JA. Tradition and innovation in scientists' research strategies. American Sociological Review 80:875-908.
records.evidence_note: Community bridging is a research strategy signal; it requires a historically frozen knowledge network and is not interchangeable with pair novelty.

records.citation: Wang Z, Zhang H, Chen J, Chen H. An effective framework for measuring the novelty of scientific articles through integrated topic modeling and cloud model. Journal of Informetrics 18:101587.
records.evidence_note: Topic-model/cloud-model family; locally unavailable without frozen text and trained models.

records.citation: Wu W, Zhang C, Zhao Y. Automated novelty evaluation of academic paper: a collaborative approach integrating human and large language model knowledge. JASIST 76:1452-1469.
records.evidence_note: A judgment system rather than a fixed mathematical indicator under the present reproducibility boundary.

records.citation: Kruzenshtern A, Dodonov V, Chechurin L. AI-based metric for scientific text novelty. World Conference of AI-Powered Innovation and TRIZ Methodology:367-378.
records.evidence_note: Token surprise and semantic-gain families require frozen historical language models.

records.citation: Kruzenshtern A, Dodonov V, Chechurin L. Domain agnostic features for robust novelty assessment of scientific publication. Scientometrics.
records.evidence_note: Cross-domain application is recent and still requires unavailable historical models in the local corpus.

records.citation: Peng X, et al. SemNovel: a new approach to detecting semantic novelty of biomedical publications using embeddings of large language models. Journal of Biomedical Informatics 172:104952.
records.evidence_note: Biomedical LLM-embedding framework; modality and model are not frozen locally.

records.citation: Stirling A. A general framework for analysing diversity in science, technology and society. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 4:707-719.
records.evidence_note: Separates variety, balance, and disparity; it does not establish them as novelty indicators.

records.citation: Wang J, Thijs B, Glänzel W. Interdisciplinarity and impact: distinct effects of variety, balance, and disparity. PLOS ONE 10:e0127298.
records.evidence_note: Shows that diversity components behave differently; citation association is not novelty validation.

records.citation: Rafols I, Meyer M. Diversity and network coherence as indicators of interdisciplinarity. Scientometrics 82:263-287.
records.evidence_note: Diversity, integration, and coherence are interdisciplinarity constructs.

records.citation: Leydesdorff L, Wagner CS, Bornmann L. Interdisciplinarity as diversity in citation patterns among journals. Journal of Informetrics 13:255-269.
records.evidence_note: DIV and cosine-disparity family; explicitly an interdisciplinarity measurement.

records.citation: Rao CR. Diversity and dissimilarity coefficients: a unified approach. Theoretical Population Biology 21:24-43.
records.evidence_note: Original quadratic entropy; not a scientific-novelty source.

records.citation: Hill MO. Diversity and evenness: a unifying notation and its consequences. Ecology 54:427-432.
records.evidence_note: Effective-number diversity family; not a novelty construct.

records.citation: Pielou EC. Shannon's formula as a measure of specific diversity: its use and misuse. American Naturalist 100:463-465.
records.evidence_note: Evenness source; not a novelty source.

records.citation: Porter AL, Cohen AS, Roessner JD, Perreault M. Measuring researcher interdisciplinarity. Scientometrics 72:117-147.
records.evidence_note: Integration score belongs to interdisciplinarity measurement.

records.citation: Funk RJ, Owen-Smith J. A dynamic network measure of technological change. Management Science 63:791-817.
records.evidence_note: Disruption requires future citations and measures later knowledge-flow change.

records.citation: Teplitskiy M, Peng H, Blasco A, Lakhani KR. Is novel research worth doing? PNAS 119:e2118046119.
records.evidence_note: Independent application of atypicality and conventionality profiles.

records.citation: Yan B, Luo J. Technological novelty profile and invention's future impact. EPJ Data Science 5:2.
records.evidence_note: Exact fixed-marginal hypergeometric co-occurrence null used for a documented analytical adaptation.

records.citation: Zhou X, Zhou M, Huang D, Cui L. A probabilistic model for co-occurrence analysis in bibliometrics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics 128:104047.
records.evidence_note: Independent evaluation of an exact fixed-marginal co-occurrence model.

records.citation: ASPR v6.1 internal outcome-blind coverage, stability, temporal, toy, and formula-equivalence audit.
records.evidence_note: Supplies no construct authority; only outcome-blind local coverage and stability evidence is reused.
